comment: The rules of D3.5 and D6.9 that close two routes to a forged pointer. The `.ptr` of a span or a
string stands in two positions only, each as it stands: an argument of an `extern fn`, fixed or
in the variable tail, and an operand of `==` or `!=`. No cast and no `str.from_cstr` takes a
`.ptr` (D3.5). Only a trusted module declares or calls an `extern fn`, and its rows state what C
gives back (D9.8). Only `str.from_cstr` and `rt.args_init` take `p[lo..hi]` of a raw pointer,
and no source names `rt.args_init` (D6.9). The rows cover src/fort/check.ft: pseudo_field,
ptr_node, the arguments of check_call, the operands of `==` and `!=` in check_expr,
raw_span_allowed, is_args_init, check_span_expr and value_of_sym. Three rows hold the callee of
a call: check_call reads the symbol of the callee node and gives it to the result, so a call
through a function pointer that a call gives names no function, and the `&` of check_unary reads
its operand node. The first stage runs the language tests of the two rules, whose goldens pin
each message and its position. The second runs check_raw_span_test.ft, which holds the two
functions in a sandbox std. The table runs in the VM with the debug preset: pass a --runner that
runs tools/vm run in one slot, as notes/environment.md says. The md5 guard reads the product
compiler. The first round of a run in the VM can read stale (notes/testing.md 1), so run the
first row again before you trust it.
build: sleep 2 && touch src/fort/check.ft && ninja -C build/Linux/debug fort

stages.name: the language tests of the two rules
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std -j 4 fail/spans/007 fail/stdlib/007 fail/stdlib/008 fail/pointers/009 fail/pointers/010 fail/pointers/005 fail/ffi/013 fail/ffi/014 fail/ffi/015 run/ffi/020 run/pointers/004 run/pointers/014 run/stdlib/013 run/stdlib/068 run/stdlib/125 run/stdlib/126

stages.name: the checker suite of the two functions
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 300 -j 2 check_raw_span_test

mutations.what: no argument of an `extern fn` takes a `.ptr`
an argument of a fort function and of a function pointer takes a `.ptr`

mutations.new:
if (ptr_legal && i < f.ty->params.len) {
            ck->ptr_ok = ptr_node(ast.ast_child(n, i));
mutations.what: no argument of the variable tail takes a `.ptr`
a `.ptr` that `->` reaches is no argument of an `extern fn`
an extern call in a module that is not trusted reports its `.ptr` too
a call through the function pointer that an extern call gives is a call of that extern
`&` of the result of a call takes the address of the function that the call names
the result of a call through a value names the function of the call that gave the value
the left operand of `==` and `!=` takes no `.ptr`
the right operand of `==` and `!=` takes no `.ptr`
each function takes `p[lo..hi]` of a raw pointer
